outcome: Experiment Authoring now links compiler diagnostics to source and offers constrained completion
owner_impact: Configuration, Initialization, Controller and Metrics errors now remain attached to their artifact and appear in the active editor with source-line gutter markers where the compiler provides a location. Selecting a diagnostic jumps to that source line. Controller, Metrics and Initialization expose lightweight completion derived only from implemented compiler/capability/configuration surfaces; no unrestricted Python language server or AI code generation was added. Existing source, dirty-state, autosave, revision and runtime semantics are unchanged.

next.text: The currently approved #202 code-authoring ergonomics epic is complete with #205. No further ticket in this epic is approved or queued.

technical_evidence: Authoring diagnostics are produced by the existing Configuration, Initializer, Controller, Environment, Metrics and runtime validators, normalized only for presentation, and retained by artifact identity.
Ace consumes exact compiler line/column locations through session annotations; the visible diagnostic detail is keyboard-accessible and selection reuses the existing source-line navigation path.

Controller completion is exported from the compiler's implemented call signatures, observations and active numeric parameters; Metrics completion uses compiler call signatures and directly insertable snapshot fields; Initializer completion uses parsed functions and active config parameters.
Browser and MCP Controller/Metrics compiler copies remain byte-identical after exposing completion metadata.

Production smoke opens Ace completion, injects a temporary Controller syntax error, verifies the linked gutter annotation and diagnostic jump, restores the source, and requires the annotation to clear before continuing runtime smoke.
